sections.overview: Geotrupes stercorarius is a European dung beetle that tunnels beneath dung and is often called the common earth-boring dung beetle.
sections.identification: It is a robust, dark beetle with a metallic sheen; German accounts give a body length of 15–27 mm and seven strong longitudinal grooves on each elytron. A fresh specimen has a stronger metallic sheen than the similar G. spiniger.
sections.habitat: It uses open, sparsely vegetated ground as well as woodland paths and forest, and has been recorded at elevations up to 2,300 m.
sections.diet: Adults feed on dung, especially that of cattle and horses.
sections.behavior: Adults tunnel and bury dung; a 2026 experiment found that simulated warming altered tunnel depth and dung-burial behaviour.
sections.reproduction: In Geotrupes, mated females excavate nesting burrows; the exact details of the species’ life cycle are not fully summarized in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: It is a tunnelling dung beetle, unlike ball-rolling scarabaeine dung beetles; it can be confused with the related G. spiniger, which Italian keys distinguish partly by elevation and underside characters.
sections.conservation: A German specialist site reports that it has become scarce in several regions, but this is a regional observation rather than a global assessment.
